justifications.c1: Independent per-incident figures far above £5k: KI's SEK 30m rebuild compensation (search-confirmed), the $14.975m Pacific Fertility jury verdict (several sources) and ATCC cell-line panels at $4.8–5.3k; but both big losses were auto-fill or tank-defect failures, not missed top-ups of standalone dewars, and per-site annual loss is unquantified.
justifications.c2: Weekly refill per tank is recommended by CFAS guidance (search-confirmed) and a USPTO patent describes daily visual and dipstick checks as standard practice; the peer-reviewed weight study shows boil-off is measurable within days, but no per-dewar failure rate exists and CFAS is fertility-specific guidance.
justifications.c3: Documented workarounds: daily visual/dipstick checks (patent), BOC Cryospeed scheduled delivery, wired low-level alarms ($1,476 Thermo; NZ$5,143 Cryo-Sentry) and subscription monitors; technician labour is not quantified.
justifications.c4: CFAS guidance says every cryo tank 'must' have a temperature or level sensor with external call-out (search-confirmed, Canada, fertility only); KI's reviews criticised alarm handling; no UK HTA or research-lab rule was pinned and no insurer condition was found.
justifications.c5: Specific titles with budget evidence: QMUL Cryostorage Facility Manager advert, Harvard freezer-core manager JD including budgeting and rate-setting, KCL facility manager with budget management, NHS Cryostore Supervisor.
justifications.c6: Lab distributors already list comparable LN2 monitoring in catalogues (VWR UK low-level alarms, Fisher TraceableLIVE with subscription) and BOC schedules LN2 drops, but no evidence the gas supplier resells monitors (recorded not found).
justifications.c7: Crowded, including weight-based incumbents: Networked Robotics, CryoScout/CryoGuardian, Columbia deployment, plus Planer, Sonicu ($595.60 kit), Fisher ($80–100/yr), XiltriX and SmartCap; the remaining gap (published-price cellular weight platform for small fleets) is narrow and asserted.
justifications.c8: Load-cell kits (HX711 ~$8, hobby-grade) and nRF9160 LTE-M modules ($27–38) are priced and lab mains power is available, but 0.02 kg resolution under heavy dewars, a robust platform, near-real-time alerts for <3-minute losses and cellular coverage in basement cryostores are unproven.
justifications.c9: Comparable subscriptions are evidenced (Fisher $80–100/device/yr; Minus80 $213/yr per unit at Mount Sinai) and ongoing alarm-test records have value, but there is no statutory or insurer record schedule for UK research dewars.
justifications.c10: Institutional reviews (KI internal and external reports), trade press (Nordic Life Science, Life Science Sweden), national news (The Local, Phys.org, NBC, WION), peer-reviewed studies and litigation (jury verdict, 550+ legal actions); no forum complaints found.

weakest: Weight-based and wireless LN2 dewar monitoring already exists from several vendors (Networked Robotics, CryoScout, Planer, Sonicu, Fisher) at modest subscription prices, so the market gap is narrow and only asserted.
